events.summary: One-shot: Online + family bulletin: 94.9% ± 4.7 vs 48.0% ± 18.2 for current practice (% of working parents who heard within 3 days). OS one-shot: online + family bulletin wins on the measured outcome: 94.9% ± 4.7 of working parents heard within 3 days versus 48.0% ± 18.2 for current practice. It also holds up on held-out tests, staying at 90.2%–96.1% versus 46.4%–57.0% for current practice, so the gain is large and consistent.
events.assumptions: This depends on the synthetic resident schedules, arrival patterns, and word-of-mouth rates used by the model. It also assumes the bulletin channel exists in practice, even though the local sources only explicitly confirm online channels.
events.pilot: Run a 2-week pilot for one district notice: post online and send the family bulletin once, then measure the share of working parents reached within 3 days and compare it with the prior notice process.
